key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells do more than manage light: they can also improve film formation, crystal quality, charge extraction, and mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: Texture engineering is a multi-functional design strategy that can raise efficiency and device durability in perovskite photovoltaics and related optoelectronic devices.
method: Use nano-/micro-textured interfaces to reduce reflection and boost light trapping.
Promote better wetting of perovskite precursor solutions for more uniform film deposition.
Leverage texture-driven changes in crystallinity, carrier extraction, and flexibility for device gains.
evidence_signal: The paper is a review of very recently reported studies, synthesizing reported improvements in wetting, crystallinity, open-circuit voltage, and mechanical stability rather than presenting a single new experimental dataset.
watch_item: Texture benefits may depend strongly on fabrication compatibility and trade-offs between optical gains, film quality, and mechanical integrity across different device stacks.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
